hitl_conditions: Role and data resolution depend on organisational level: managers/planners receive coarse statistical indicators for strategic/planning decisions; schedulers/operators receive fine operational data for task assignment and onsite dispatch; authorised users access other levels remotely; during COVID-19 local operators decided decentrally.

hitl_decision_levels.who: manager & vice manager who operate the entire logistics processes
hitl_decision_levels.data_resolution: coarsest, abstract statistical indicators (3D-detailed DT visualization is 'data overload' for them)

hitl_decision_levels.who: planning department at headquarters coordinating local divisions nationwide
hitl_decision_levels.data_resolution: statistical indicator data to coordinate planning, execution and scheduling (simulation and optimization)
hitl_decision_levels.decision_type: systematically optimized planning decisions; 'face the most complicated situations'

hitl_decision_levels.data_resolution: finer operational data (statistical, coarse-grained data is 'underload' for onsite scheduling)
hitl_decision_levels.decision_type: assign operational tasks within their own divisions

hitl_decision_levels.who: frontline operation departments at manufacturers and warehouses, subordinate to schedulers
hitl_decision_levels.data_resolution: finest: operational detailed data (3D visualization, simulation); black-box detail 'more valuable for the onsite operators than the schedulers'
hitl_decision_levels.decision_type: execute schedulers' instructions; onsite dispatch now tracked online via the DT; during COVID-19 given 'the ability to make decentralized decisions'

hitl_decision_levels.systems: DigiPyramid DSI interface plus each level's operational systems
hitl_decision_levels.data_resolution: 18 AHP-weighted decision-support indicators from a questionnaire answered by users at the four levels (Table 1), adjusted dynamically per scenario
hitl_decision_levels.decision_type: with authorization a user can access other levels' interfaces for remote operations; AI (BN/CV) only completes ambiguous data, decisions stay with humans
hitl_decision_levels.source: Sec. III-A; III-D1; IV-B; V-B; V-C

key_finding: Implemented multiresolution logistics twin (DigiPyramid) for a Chinese nationwide logistics firm: RPA aggregates ERP/WMS/TMS data, Bayesian networks and computer vision fill 'breakpoints', 'gray boxes' and 'black boxes', and AHP-derived indicators serve four human decision levels (managers, planners, schedulers, operators); humans keep all decisions, AI only improves twin fidelity.

quotes.text: The DigiPyramid proposed in this article was a low-cost and flexible DT framework for Company Z, a Chinese nationwide logistics enterprise.

The DigiPyramid employed BN-based algorithms to eliminate the ambiguity of “breakpoints” and “gray boxes.” For example, according to the malfunction of a device, the possibility can be inferred by the probability a priori by training the previous datasets.
DigiPyramid employed CV algorithms to analyze the monitoring video data on platform operation, opening the “black box” to some extent.

Nowadays, AI and optimization approaches replace humans in automatically making operational decisions. However, most decisions still rely on personal experience of human operators [5], [9]. On the other side, different-level operators require different resolutions and data granularity for their decision-making.

The hierarchical structure of decision chains in the distributed logistics process management formed a pyramid-like organization structure, containing four levels from top to bottom, namely, managers, planners, schedulers, and operators (as shown in Fig. 1).
In addition, the DT platform also provided the local operators with the ability to make decentralized decisions.
